title: Energy Flow and Matter Cycling
seo_title: Energy Pyramid Worksheets: Trophic Levels and the 10% Rule (High School Biology)
standard_text: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for the cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions. Use mathematical representations to support claims for the cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on energy flow in ecosystems (NGSS HS-LS2-3, HS-LS2-4): trophic levels, the 10% rule, energy pyramids, decomposers and matter cycling. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: About 10% of the energy passes to each higher level.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy flows up and is lost; matter cycles.

  • About 10% of the energy passes to the next level; about 90% leaves as heat and waste.
  • Carbon and nitrogen cycle through producers, consumers, decomposers and the air.
Example

Grass: 20,000 kJ. Energy for mice (3rd level)?

÷10 twice

20,000 → 2,000 → 200

Answer: 200 kJ

Example

Why are hawks rare?

Little energy at the top

Answer: Not enough energy to support many

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled. Matter is recycled; energy is lost as heat.
  • Passing on 90% instead of 10%.
  • Thinking top predators have the most energy.

faq.a: About 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next; the rest is used for life processes and lost as heat.

faq.q: Why is energy lost at each level?
faq.a: Organisms use most of the energy in cellular respiration, which releases heat, and some is lost in waste.
Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste, returning carbon, nitrogen and other nutrients to the air and soil.
